title: Blackjack Simplified
story: 21. The magic number. Get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over. Aces are 1 or 11. Face cards are 10. Hit or stand — every decision risks busting. Build the casino classic that's been dealt on felt tables for centuries.
why: Blackjack combines card values, ace flexibility (1 or 11), dealer AI logic, win/loss/push outcomes, and hand comparison — rich game logic in a compact program.
analogy: A high-stakes tug-of-war with 21 as the cliff edge. Pull too hard (hit) and you might fall off (bust). Pull too little (stand) and the dealer might pull past you. Your Blackjack code is the rope: every card pulls you closer to 21 or over the edge.
try_it: Add betting: start with 100 chips, bet before each hand, win = double bet, blackjack = 1.5x. Add 'split' for pairs. Add card counting tracking (running count of high vs low cards). Simulate 1000 hands and calculate the house edge.
tips: Ace is 11 by default, but becomes 1 if total would exceed 21
Dealer must hit on 16 or less, stand on 17 or more — it's automatic
Blackjack = Ace + 10-value card = exactly 21 in 2 cards
common_mistakes: Counting all Aces as 11 and busting on Ace+Ace — should be 12 not 22
Dealer standing on soft 17 (Ace+6) — some casinos hit, some stand
Comparing values before checking for bust — bust ALWAYS loses regardless
